faq.title: Why am I suddenly getting missed video calls on WhatsApp from +84, +62, or +234?
faq.description: These calls originate from transnational cyber fraud syndicates operating out of Southeast Asia and Africa. They use automated VoIP bots to place thousands of 1-second missed calls simultaneously. When curious victims call back, the scammers initiate lucrative investment scams, fake part-time YouTube rating tasks, or blackmail attempts.

faq.title: What happens if I accidentally answer an international spam call?
faq.description: Answering does not instantly hack your smartphone. However, answering confirms to the automated bot dialer that your telephone number is active and monitored by a live human. Your number is immediately upgraded to high-value target lists on dark web lead registries, causing an exponential surge in subsequent spam calls and phishing SMS messages.

faq.title: Can Indian telecom operators (Jio, Airtel, Vi) block international calls by default?
faq.description: Yes. Following Department of Telecommunications (DoT) directives, Indian carriers now deploy International Incoming Spoofed Calling Prevention Systems. Additionally, users can request their telecom operator to place a permanent incoming International Long Distance (ILD) bar on their cellular SIM line.

html:
The Surge of Foreign VoIP Call Scams in India

Over the past 24 months, tens of millions of smartphone users across India have experienced an unprecedented bombardment of unexpected international voice and video calls. You glance at your phone and observe missed calls from country codes you have never dialed: +84 (Vietnam), +62 (Indonesia), +234 (Nigeria), +254 (Kenya), +60 (Malaysia), or +1 (virtual North American VoIP numbers). Often, the caller disconnects after a single ring (a classic 'Wangiri' trap), or sends an automated WhatsApp message offering '₹3,000 per day for liking YouTube videos and rating Google Maps hotels'.

These calls are not accidental wrong numbers. They represent the frontline operational vector of heavily organized, industrial-scale cybercrime syndicates. Using automated computer-generated Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) dialers, these syndicates blast millions of Indian mobile numbers harvested from compromised telecom databases, e-commerce breaches, and public registries. This comprehensive guide details the mechanics of international VoIP fraud and provides the concrete steps to permanently silence and block these predatory calls across both WhatsApp and cellular networks.

Deconstructing the 3 Most Common International Call Scams

Understanding the psychological levers and financial traps deployed by these syndicates is the key to safeguarding your household:

  1. The 'Part-Time Task' / Telegram Recruitment Trap: The call connects or leaves a voice message from a supposed human resources recruiter representing global marketing firms. The victim is instructed to message an executive on Telegram, where they are paid ₹150 for 'liking' three YouTube videos as an initial hook. Once trust is established, the victim is lured into high-stakes 'cryptocurrency merchant rating tasks' where they are pressured to invest lakhs of rupees into fabricated web portals that freeze their funds.
  2. The Wangiri (One-Ring) Callback Trap: The automated system rings your cellular phone for exactly 1.5 seconds and terminates. Curious users who dial back the unfamiliar international number are routed to premium-rate satellite or international telephone services that bill exorbitant charges (often ₹100 to ₹300 per minute), with the proceeds split between corrupt telecom operators and the scammers.
  3. Video Call Extortion (Sextortion Schemes): The incoming WhatsApp call is a video call featuring a seductive profile photo. If the victim accepts the video call, the caller immediately displays pre-recorded explicit video footage while recording the victim's face on split-screen. Within minutes, the victim receives threatening WhatsApp messages demanding immediate UPI ransoms under threat of publishing the edited video to family members and Facebook friends.

Method 1: Enabling WhatsApp's Native International Call Shield

In response to the epidemic of spam calling, WhatsApp introduced a dedicated setting that silences calls from unknown numbers automatically without notifying you in real-time:

  1. Open WhatsApp on your smartphone.
  2. Tap the three vertical dots in the upper right-hand corner (or tap Settings in the lower bar on iOS) and select Settings.
  3. Tap Privacy.
  4. Scroll down the privacy menu and select Calls.
  5. Locate the toggle titled Silence unknown callers and switch it strictly to ON.

What happens when this feature is active?

When an incoming call originates from any phone number that is not saved in your personal smartphone address book—including every single foreign country code (+84, +62, +234, etc.):

  • Your smartphone screen will never illuminate or ring.
  • Your device will not vibrate, allowing you to sleep or work without disruption.
  • The call will still be logged silently in your WhatsApp 'Calls' tab marked as 'Silenced unknown caller', allowing you to verify if a legitimate delivery driver or service agent was trying to reach you.

Method 2: Configuring Android's Native Dialer Spam Engine

To eliminate international spam calls arriving over standard cellular carrier lines (Jio, Airtel, Vi, and BSNL), leverage the Google Phone app's algorithmic spam shield:

  1. Open the standard Phone app (by Google) on your Android device.
  2. Tap the three vertical dots in the search bar and select Settings.
  3. Tap Caller ID & spam.
  4. Ensure 'See caller and spam ID' is enabled.
  5. Toggle on 'Filter spam calls'. When active, Google's global telemetry network automatically drops calls identified as suspected fraud or telemarketing before your phone rings.
  6. For complete peace of mind: Navigate to Settings > Blocked numbers and toggle on Unknown. This blocks all calls from private, unidentified, or spoofed international numbers that hide their Caller Line Identification (CLI).

Method 3: Filing Complaints via DoT Chakshu (Sanchar Saathi Portal)

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) operates a centralized citizen intelligence facility called Chakshu, designed specifically to report suspected fraudulent communications before financial loss occurs:

  1. Open your browser and navigate to the official portal: https://sanchar-saathi.gov.in.
  2. Click on Citizen Centric Services and select Chakshu - Report Suspected Fraud Communication.
  3. Select the medium of communication (Call / SMS / WhatsApp).
  4. Select the suspected fraud category: choose 'Fake Job / Part-Time Offer', 'Impersonation of Government / Police', or 'International Call with Indian CLI'.
  5. Upload a screenshot of the WhatsApp call log displaying the international country code and timestamp.
  6. Enter the offending foreign phone number and submit the form with your verified mobile OTP.

Submitting reports to Chakshu allows telecom authorities to track the upstream VoIP gateways routing these calls into Indian telecom circles and issue block orders across national internet gateways.

Technical Deep Dive: How International VoIP Spoofing Works

You might wonder: how can an overseas criminal syndicate call tens of thousands of Indian smartphones every hour without incurring crippling international telecom charges? The answer lies in Unregulated SIP Trunking and Gray VoIP Gateways.

Modern telecommunications rely heavily on Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) to transmit voice packets over the internet. Legitimate businesses use virtual Private Branch Exchange (PBX) systems like Asterisk or FreeSWITCH to manage corporate call centers. However, criminal operators purchase wholesale VoIP termination minutes from shady offshore providers operating in jurisdictions with lax telecom oversight.

Through these gateways, scammers exploit a vulnerability in legacy signaling protocols: the ability to arbitrarily alter the Caller Line Identification (CLI) field in the SIP header. When the VoIP server transmits an invitation packet (SIP INVITE), it inserts a spoofed number into the From: display field. As the packet traverses international undersea fiber cables and enters Indian national gateways, legacy telecom switches often fail to perform cryptographic origin validation (STIR/SHAKEN), forwarding the spoofed number directly to your mobile tower.

Method 4: Prefix Regex Filtering on Android with Open-Source Tools

While WhatsApp allows you to silence all unknown callers, you may still want to receive legitimate calls from unknown domestic Indian numbers (such as couriers, cab drivers, or hospital receptionists) while strictly blacklisting foreign prefixes (+84, +62, +234, +254, etc.). You can achieve this using prefix wildcard blocking:

  1. Install an open-source, offline call-filtering application such as Yet Another Call Blocker (YACB) from F-Droid or Google Play.
  2. Open the app settings and navigate to Blocking Rules.
  3. Select Add Regular Expression Rule (Regex).
  4. Input the following wildcard rules to intercept the most aggressive syndicates:
    • ^\+84.* (Blocks all incoming traffic from Vietnam)
    • ^\+62.* (Blocks all incoming traffic from Indonesia)
    • ^\+234.* (Blocks all incoming traffic from Nigeria)
    • ^\+254.* (Blocks all incoming traffic from Kenya)
    • ^\+1[0-9]{10} (Blocks unassigned North American virtual VoIP ranges)
  5. Set the action to Drop / Hang Up Silently. When a scam call arrives matching these prefixes, your phone terminates the connection at the radio interface level without ringing.

Method 5: Telecom Carrier Level ILD Barring (Jio, Airtel, Vi)

If you never expect legitimate phone calls from overseas family or business contacts, you can request your mobile carrier to place an absolute International Long Distance (ILD) bar on your SIM profile:

  • Reliance Jio: Open the MyJio app > tap your mobile profile > Settings > Service Settings > International Roaming / Calls. Ensure incoming and outgoing international roaming services are disabled.
  • Bharti Airtel: Open the Airtel Thanks app > Manage > International Services > toggle international calling to Inactive.
  • Vodafone Idea (Vi): Dial 198 from your registered Vi SIM card, connect to a customer care officer, and explicitly request: 'Please place a permanent incoming international voice and SMS bar on my connection.'

Summary Comparison: Spam Defense Mechanisms

Defense Layer Coverage Scope Device Interruption Setup Difficulty
WhatsApp Silence Unknown Callers All WhatsApp audio & video calls Zero ringing; silent log only 10 seconds (Single toggle)

What to Do If You Lost Money to an International Syndicate

If you were deceived into transferring money through a part-time job scam, task investment scheme, or extortion threat, time is of the essence. You have a critical 'Golden Hour' window to initiate bank-level transaction freezes:

  • Immediately dial 1930 (National Cyber Crime Helpline) from your mobile phone. Provide the transaction reference number (UTR), sending bank account, recipient account/UPI ID, and exact timestamp.
  • Log on to cybercrime.gov.in and register a formal cyber complaint following our comprehensive guide on how to report online fraud on the 1930 portal.
  • Read our step-by-step tutorial on stopping random scammers from adding you to WhatsApp and Telegram groups to permanently cut off group recruitment pipelines.
  • Review our checklist on 7 vital WhatsApp privacy settings you must enable today.
